messages:
alex: heads up — after the compact-run last night we're seeing a bunch of tiny workloads stuck pending on eu-west1-gpu nodes. looks like the scheduler tie-breaker for slab packing is preferring larger shape continuity and leaving 1GPU pods stranded :eyes:
maria: I saw that too, noticed a spike in pending for 1g/1c gpu pods around 03:12 UTC. tests show binpack score + shape affinity wins over 'min-fragment' heuristic.
alex: here's an example from the drain logs and pod status: 
```
NODE: gpu-node-eu-12
Pods: big-train (4g), big-train-2 (4g), small-worker (1g) Pending
kubectl describe pod small-worker
  Events:
  FailedScheduling: 0/12 nodes are available: 3 InsufficientMemory, 9 InsufficientGPU.
```
santi: so scheduler preferred keeping the 4g gang together instead of placing small-worker into a partially free node? that's the slab tie-breaker behaviour we rolled in with the compact defrager, right?
cheng: yep, the compact/shape-preserve tie-breaker was added to reduce hot-swap churn for big jobs — it biases toward co-locating similar shapes. unintended side-effect: when fragmentation is interleaved it refuses to split a node to fit 1g pods even if there's room slot-wise.
alex: cost impact: small jobs wait longer and either backfill tries to provision more nodes or we trigger on-demand -> higher spend. saw a +18% burst in provisioning requests during the window.
maria: quick mitigation options: 1) relax the slab tie-breaker threshold for eu-west1 for the next 6h, 2) allow a preemptible small-job backfill policy that can evict tail of big-gangs, 3) force defrag pass to coalesce free slots (risky).
santi: I'd prefer option 1 + metric watch. we can flip the flag per-region. I'll prepare a canary toggle.
cheng: PR to change the scheduler scoring param: `--shape-preserve-weight` from 80 -> 40 for eu-west1. also add a temporary rule to let 1g pods use 'smeared' slots when fragmentation < 60%.
alex: can you also add a short-lived alert for pending-1g > 5 across region (5m). we need to avoid cascading node provisioning.
infra-bot: Deploy plan created: toggle/shape-weight-eu-west1 -> draft. Approvers: @maria, @cheng. CI: unit + integration scheduling-sim.
maria: I'll review the PR now. can we run scheduler-sim with the eu-west1 trace first? want to validate 95th p99 placement latency.
santi: sim running (trace 2026-03-19). preliminary looks good — pending 1g goes down ~78% at cost of +1.2% placement churn for 4g jobs.
alex: ok let's canary the flag for next 2h starting in 30m. rollout plan: 1) flag in canary AZ 2) monitor pending-1g, provision rate, preempt events 3) roll to region if green.
maria: noted. if anything weird @santi will revert. :+1:
cheng: I've pushed the PR and linked the rollout playbook. tagging infra-bot to kick canary at 1777777830.
infra-bot: Canary started in eu-west1-a at 1777777830. Monitoring: pending-1g, provision-rate, evictions.
alex: thanks. will follow up with cost delta after 4h. if we still see fragmentation I'll open a deeper ticket for a defrag job that does non-disruptive compaction (kv-cache aware).
maria: thanks all — good canary cadence.
cheng: follow-up note: long-term we should consider a shape-aware reclamation that can split big-gangs into two smaller allocations during low-util windows to reduce fragmentation without increasing evictions. added to backlog. :memo:
